title: Alterations in Running Biomechanics after 12 Week Gait Retraining with Minimalist Shoes
publisher: International Journal of Environmental Research and Public Health
claims: Thirty male recreational runners were randomly assigned to 12 weeks of gait retraining plus minimalist shoes (n=15) or minimalist shoes alone (n=15); 17 completed the training.
The combined programme converted rearfoot strikers into forefoot strikers at a rate of 78% (7/9).
Loading rate decreased significantly in both groups, and the gait-retraining group had a lower loading rate than the minimalist-shoe-only group.
Foot strike angle decreased significantly only in the gait-retraining group; ankle joint moment increased in that group.
Vertical stiffness of the lower limb improved significantly in both groups.
The authors conclude that minimalist footwear alone may have limited effects on reducing running-related impact.

verification.note: 经 Europe PMC 全文 XML 读取 Methods/Results/Conclusion 正文，非仅摘要。

claimVerification.note: 原文：“Thirty participants were randomly (random number sort) divided into gait retraining + minimalist shoe (GR) and minimalist shoe (MIN) groups”；“Seventeen participants completed intervention and met the inclusion criteria (nine in the GR group, eight in the MIN group)”。15/组与 17 人完成均一致。
原文结论：“The 12 week gait retraining with minimalist shoes converted rearfoot strikers into forefoot strikers with a rate of 78% (7/9).”

原文：“the loading rate … was significantly reduced by 22.6% (GR) and 17.2% (MIN) after training (p < 0.001, p = 0.017). The loading rate of the GR group was lower than that of the MIN group after training (p = 0.015).”
原文：GR 组 foot-strike angle 减少约 10.3°，MIN 组无差异；“the peak moment was increased by 17.8% after training in the GR group (p = 0.001)”，MIN 组无变化（指踝关节峰值力矩）。

原文：“A significant main effect of time was observed on vertical stiffness (p = 0.035). After training, the vertical stiffness improved in the GR and MIN groups by 17.2% and 7.1%, respectively”；未报告 time×group 交互，即显著性来自时间主效应而非各组单独检验。
原文：“these observations also suggest that the sole use of minimalist footwear may have limited effects on reducing running-related impacts.”
